proposed_english: rise up against / convey upward against
rationale: The standard upward-conveyance verb ⲭⲉⲥⲧ (already in glossary) here takes adversative ⲟⲩⲃⲉ 'against' — denoting hostile ascent rather than salvific elevation. Worth noting as a marked usage in the cosmogonic register.

Compound ⲡⲛⲁⲟ ('great') + ⲛⲉⲟ̄ unidentified element. Stands in parallel with ⲡⲙⲓϣⲉ 'the battle' in line 28. Possibly a Lyc reflex or scribal variant of an attested cosmic-combat term. Flag for parallels.
Lyc reflex of ϩⲁ-ⲡⲣⲟ 'at the face/door of' = 'before.' Used here temporally: 'before eternity.' Spatial-temporal preposition standard in Lycopolitan.
Lyc reflex of ϫⲱⲗϫ̄/ϫⲱⲗⲕ̄ 'mingle, twist together.' Parallel to ⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ in same passage; both verbs describe the cosmic interpenetration of light and darkness.

Greek loanword ἐνθύμησις. Already attested in the five-faculty mapping (corresponding to ⲡⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ 'counsel'). Here used cosmologically of a personified Thought operating in the land of darkness — possibly the Enthumesis of Death, a Manichaean technical figure for matter's reflective principle.
